title.en: Biographies of Fu, Jin, and the Marquis of Kuaicheng
title.raw: 《傅靳蒯成列傳》 Biographies of Fu, Jin, and the Marquis of Kuaicheng

sentences.zh: 陽陵侯傅寬，以魏五大夫騎將從，為舍人，起橫陽。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yangling, Fu Kuan, followed as a Wei cavalry general holding the rank of Fifth-Rank Grandee, became a retainer, and first rose at Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Yangling, Fu Kuan, had held the Wei rank of Fifth-Rank Grandee and served as a cavalry general. He joined as a retainer, first rising at Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 從攻安陽、杠裏，擊趙賁軍於開封，及擊楊熊曲遇、陽武，斬首十二級，賜爵卿。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Anyang and Gangli, struck Zhao Ben's army at Kaifeng, and also struck Yang Xiong at Quyu and Yangwu. He took twelve heads and was granted the noble rank of Minister (qing).
translations.idiomatic: Fu Kuan took part in the attacks on Anyang and Gangli, engaged Zhao Ben's army at Kaifeng, and fought Yang Xiong at Quyu and Yangwu. He took twelve heads and was granted the rank of Minister.

sentences.zh: 從至霸上。

translations.literal: He followed and arrived at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: The army then reached Bashang.

sentences.zh: 沛公立為漢王，漢王賜寬封號共德君。

translations.literal: When Pei Gong was established as Han King, the Han King granted Fu Kuan the title Lord Gongde.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Pei was made King of Han, the king bestowed upon Fu Kuan the title Lord of Shared Virtue.

sentences.zh: 從入漢中，遷為右騎將。

translations.literal: He followed in entering Hanzhong and was promoted to Right Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: From there he followed the king into Hanzhong and was promoted to General of the Right Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從定三秦，賜食邑雕陰。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Three Qins and was granted the fief of Diaoyin.
translations.idiomatic: During the pacification of the Three Qin kingdoms, he was granted the revenue fief of Diaoyin.

sentences.zh: 從擊項籍，待懷，賜爵通德侯。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Xiang Ji, waited at Huai, and was granted the title Marquis of Tongde.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Xiang Ji, he was stationed at Huai and granted the title Marquis of Tongde.

sentences.zh: 從擊項冠、周蘭、龍且，所將卒斬騎將一人敖下，益食邑。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Ju. The troops he led beheaded one cavalry general below Ao, and his fief was increased.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaigns against Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Ju. The troops under his command beheaded a cavalry general at Ao, and his fief was enlarged.

sentences.zh: 屬淮陰，擊破齊歷下軍，擊田解。

translations.literal: He belonged to Huaiyin, struck and broke the Qi army at Lixia, and struck Tian Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under the Marquis of Huaiyin, he shattered the Qi army at Lixia and defeated Tian Jie.

sentences.zh: 屬相國參，殘博，益食邑。

translations.literal: He belonged to Chancellor Cao Shen, massacred Bo, and his fief was increased.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Chancellor Cao Shen, he ravaged Bo, and his fief was enlarged.

sentences.zh: 因定齊地，剖符世世勿絕，封為陽陵侯，二千六百戶，除前所食。

translations.literal: Therefore, having pacified Qi territory, he was given a split tally for perpetual inheritance, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangling with 2,600 households, with previous fiefs eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in pacifying the territory of Qi, he received a bronze tally guaranteeing his line in perpetuity and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangling with two thousand six hundred households, superseding all previous fiefs.

sentences.zh: 為齊右丞相，備齊。

translations.literal: He served as Right Chancellor of Qi and defended Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Right Chancellor of Qi and was charged with its defense.

sentences.zh: 五歲為齊相國。

translations.literal: For five years he served as Chancellor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Chancellor of Qi for five years.

sentences.zh: 四月，擊陳豨，屬太尉勃，以相國代丞相噲擊豨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he attacked Chen Xi, was subordinate to Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, and as chancellor of Qi replaced Chancellor Fan Kuai in the campaign against Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, he joined the campaign against Chen Xi under Grand Commandant Zhou Bo; as Chancellor of Qi he took Fan Kuai's place as chancellor in the attack on Xi.

sentences.zh: 一月，徙為代相國，將屯。

translations.literal: In one month, he was transferred to Chancellor of Dai and led the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After one month, he was transferred to serve as Chancellor of Dai and commanded the garrison there.

sentences.zh: 二歲，為代丞相，將屯。

translations.literal: For two years he served as Chancellor of Dai and led the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he served as Chancellor of Dai and commanded the garrison.

sentences.zh: 孝惠五年卒，謚為景侯。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Xiaohui and was posthumously named Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign and was posthumously titled Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子頃侯精立，二十四年卒。

translations.literal: His son Marquis Qing Jing succeeded him and died after twenty-four years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing succeeded him as Marquis Qing and died after twenty-four years.

sentences.zh: 子共侯則立，十二年卒。

translations.literal: His son Marquis Gong Ze succeeded him and died after twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ze succeeded him as Marquis Gong and died after twelve years.

sentences.zh: 子侯偃立，三十一年，坐與淮南王謀反，死，國除。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded him as marquis. After thirty-one years, he was implicated in plotting rebellion with the King of Huainan, was put to death, and his state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded as marquis. After thirty-one years, he was convicted of conspiring with the King of Huainan to rebel, was put to death, and his state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 信武侯靳歙，以中涓從，起宛朐。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Xinwu, Jin Xi, followed as an inner attendant and arose from Wanqu.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Xinwu, Jin Xi, joined as an inner attendant, first rising at Wanqu.

sentences.zh: 攻濟陽。

translations.literal: He attacked Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xi attacked Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 破李由軍。

translations.literal: He broke Li You's army.
translations.idiomatic: He then defeated the army of Li You.

sentences.zh: 擊秦軍亳南、開封東北，斬騎千人將一人，首五十七級，捕虜七十三人，賜爵封號臨平君。

translations.literal: He struck the Qin army south of Bo and northeast of Kaifeng, beheaded one commander of a thousand cavalry, took fifty-seven heads, captured seventy-three prisoners, and was granted a noble rank and the title Lord of Linping.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Qin army south of Bo and northeast of Kaifeng, he beheaded a commander of a thousand cavalry, took fifty-seven heads, and captured seventy-three prisoners. For this he was granted a noble rank and the title Lord of Linping.

sentences.zh: 又戰藍田北，斬車司馬二人，騎長一人，首二十八級，捕虜五十七人。

translations.literal: He again battled north of Lantian, beheaded two chariot assistant directors and one cavalry captain, took twenty-eight heads, and captured fifty-seven prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again north of Lantian, beheading two chariot marshals and one cavalry captain, taking twenty-eight heads, and capturing fifty-seven prisoners.

sentences.zh: 至霸上。

translations.literal: He arrived at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Bashang.

sentences.zh: 沛公立為漢王，賜歙爵建武侯，遷為騎都尉。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Pei was made King of Han, he granted Jin Xi the title Marquis of Jianwu and promoted him to Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After the Lord of Pei was installed as King of Han, Jin Xi received the rank of Marquis of Jianwu and was promoted to Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 從定三秦。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Three Qins.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xi took part in pacifying the Three Qin kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 別西擊章平軍於隴西，破之，定隴西六縣，所將卒斬車司馬、候各四人，騎長十二人。

translations.literal: He separately struck west against Zhang Ping's army at Longxi, broke it, pacified six counties of Longxi. The troops he led beheaded four chariot assistant directors, four scouts, and twelve cavalry captains.
translations.idiomatic: Detached westward, he attacked Zhang Ping's army at Longxi and defeated it, pacifying six counties in the region. The troops under his command beheaded four chariot marshals, four scouts, and twelve cavalry captains.

sentences.zh: 從東擊楚，至彭城。

translations.literal: He followed in striking east against Chu and arrived at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastward campaign against Chu, he reached Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 漢軍敗還，保雍丘，去擊反者王武等。

translations.literal: The Han army was defeated and returned, defended Yongqiu, and went to strike the rebels Wang Wu and others.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han army was defeated and fell back, he defended Yongqiu, then went to attack the rebel Wang Wu and his confederates.

sentences.zh: 略梁地，別將擊邢說軍菑南，破之，身得說都尉二人，司馬、候十二人，降吏卒四千一百八十人。

translations.literal: He raided Liang territory; as a detached commander he attacked Xing Shuo's army south of Zi, defeated it, personally captured two commandants of Shuo, twelve marshals and scouts, and induced the surrender of four thousand one hundred eighty officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Raiding Liang territory as a detached commander, he attacked Xing Shuo's army south of Zi and defeated it. Jin Xi personally captured two of Shuo's commandants and twelve marshals and scouts, and induced the surrender of four thousand one hundred eighty officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 破楚軍滎陽東。

translations.literal: He broke the Chu army east of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu army east of Xingyang was routed.

sentences.zh: 三年，賜食邑四千二百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was granted a fief of 4,200 households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was granted a revenue fief of four thousand two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 別之河內，擊趙將賁郝軍朝歌，破之，所將卒得騎將二人，車馬二百五十匹。

translations.literal: He separately went to Henei, struck Zhao general Ben Hao's army at Zhaoge, broke it. The troops he led captured two cavalry generals and 250 chariot horses.
translations.idiomatic: Detached to Henei, he attacked the army of the Zhao general Ben Hao at Zhaoge and defeated it. The troops under his command captured two cavalry generals and two hundred fifty chariot horses.

sentences.zh: 從攻安陽以東，至棘蒲，下七縣。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking east of Anyang, arrived at Jipu, and took seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the advance east of Anyang, reached Jipu, and took seven counties.

sentences.zh: 別攻破趙軍，得其將司馬二人，候四人，降吏卒二千四百人。

translations.literal: He separately attacked and broke the Zhao army, capturing two of its assistant directors and four scouts, and inducing the surrender of 2,400 officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On another detached operation, he attacked and defeated a Zhao army, capturing two of its marshals and four scouts, and inducing the surrender of two thousand four hundred officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 從攻下邯鄲。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking and taking Handan.
translations.idiomatic: At Handan, he took part in the assault and capture of the city.

sentences.zh: 別下平陽，身斬守相，所將卒斬兵守、郡守各一人，降鄴。

translations.literal: He separately took Pingyang, personally beheaded the defending chancellor. The troops he led beheaded one garrison commander and one commandery governor each, and induced the surrender of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate operation, he took Pingyang and personally beheaded the defending chancellor. The troops under his command beheaded one garrison commander and one commandery governor, and induced the surrender of Ye.

sentences.zh: 從攻朝歌、邯鄲，及別擊破趙軍，降邯鄲郡六縣。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Zhaoge and Handan, and separately struck and broke the Zhao army, inducing the surrender of six counties of Handan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined the attacks on Zhaoge and Handan, and separately defeated a Zhao army, inducing the surrender of six counties of Handan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 還軍敖倉，破項籍軍成皋南，擊絕楚饟道，起滎陽至襄邑。

translations.literal: He returned the army to Aocang, broke Xiang Ji's army south of Chenggao, struck and cut off Chu's grain route, from Xingyang to Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Returning the army to Aocang, he defeated Xiang Ji's forces south of Chenggao and cut off the Chu supply line from Xingyang to Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 破項冠軍魯下。

translations.literal: He broke Xiang Guan's army below Lu.
translations.idiomatic: At Lu, he defeated Xiang Guan's army.

sentences.zh: 略地東至繒、郯、下邳，南至蘄、竹邑。

translations.literal: He raided territory east to Zeng, Tan, and Xiapi, and south to Zhen and Zhuyi.
translations.idiomatic: His raids extended eastward as far as Zeng, Tan, and Xiapi, and southward to Zhen and Zhuyi.

sentences.zh: 擊項悍濟陽下。

translations.literal: He struck Xiang Han below Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiyang, he attacked Xiang Han.

sentences.zh: 還擊項籍陳下，破之。

translations.literal: He returned and struck Xiang Ji below Chen and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back, he attacked Xiang Ji at Chen and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 別定江陵，降江陵柱國、大司馬以下八人，身得江陵王，生致之雒陽，因定南郡。

translations.literal: He separately pacified Jiangling, inducing the surrender of eight persons including the Pillar of State and Grand Marshal of Jiangling. He personally captured the King of Jiangling, delivered him alive to Luoyang, and thereby pacified Nangun.
translations.idiomatic: Detached to pacify Jiangling, he induced the surrender of eight officials including the Pillar of State and the Grand Marshal. He personally captured the King of Jiangling and delivered him alive to Luoyang, thereby pacifying Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 從至陳，取楚王信，剖符世世勿絕，定食四千六百戶，號信武侯。

translations.literal: He followed and arrived at Chen, took the Chu King Xin, was given a split tally for perpetual inheritance, fixed fief of 4,600 households, and titled Xinwu Hou.
translations.idiomatic: At Chen, he followed the army in seizing Han Xin, King of Chu. He received a bronze tally guaranteeing his line in perpetuity, was granted a fixed fief of four thousand six hundred households, and was titled Marquis of Xinwu.

sentences.zh: 以騎都尉從擊代，攻韓信平城下，還軍東垣。

translations.literal: As Cavalry Commandant he followed in the campaign against Dai, attacked Han Xin below Pingcheng, and returned the army to Dongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: As Cavalry Commandant, Jin Xi followed in the campaign against Dai, attacked Han Xin below Pingcheng, and returned the army to Dongyuan.

sentences.zh: 有功，遷為車騎將軍，并將梁、趙、齊、燕、楚車騎，別擊陳豨丞相敞，破之，因降曲逆。

translations.literal: For merit, he was promoted to Chariot Cavalry General, combined leading the chariot cavalry of Liang, Zhao, Qi, Yan, and Chu. He separately struck Chen Xi's chancellor Chang, broke him, and thereby induced the surrender of Quni.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit, Jin Xi was promoted to General of Chariot and Cavalry, commanding the combined chariot and cavalry forces of Liang, Zhao, Qi, Yan, and Chu. Detached to attack Chen Xi's chancellor Chang, he defeated him and thereby induced the surrender of Quni.

sentences.zh: 從擊黥布有功，益封定食五千三百戶。

translations.literal: He followed in striking Qing Bu and had merit, so his enfeoffment was increased to a fixed fief of 5,300 households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in the campaign against Qing Bu, his fief was increased to a fixed allotment of five thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 凡斬首九十級，虜百三十二人；

translations.literal: In all he took ninety heads and captured one hundred thirty-two prisoners;
translations.idiomatic: In all, he took ninety heads and captured one hundred thirty-two prisoners;

sentences.zh: 別破軍十四，降城五十九，定郡、國各一，縣二十三；

translations.literal: Separately he broke fourteen armies, induced the surrender of fifty-nine cities, and pacified one commandery, one state, and twenty-three counties;
translations.idiomatic: In separate commands, he broke fourteen armies, induced the surrender of fifty-nine cities, and pacified one commandery, one state, and twenty-three counties;

sentences.zh: 得王、柱國各一人，二千石以下至五百石三十九人。

translations.literal: He captured one king and one Pillar of State, and thirty-nine officials from the two-thousand-bushel rank down to five hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: His captures included one king, one Pillar of State, and thirty-nine officials ranging from the two-thousand-bushel rank down to five hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 高后五年，歙卒，謚為肅侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Gao Empress Dowager, Jin Xi died and was posthumously named Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Empress Dowager Gao's reign, Jin Xi died and was posthumously titled Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 子亭代侯。

translations.literal: His son Ting succeeded as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ting succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，坐事國人過律，孝文後三年，奪侯，國除。

translations.literal: After twenty-one years, he was convicted because the people of his state had violated the law. In the third year of the Houyuan era of Emperor Wen, his marquisate was stripped and his state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-one years, he was convicted because subjects of his fief had violated the law. In the third year of the Houyuan era of Emperor Wen, his marquisate was stripped and his state abolished.

sentences.zh: 蒯成侯緤者，沛人也，姓周氏。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Zhou Xie, was a man of Pei and bore the surname Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Xie, was a man of Pei, surnamed Zhou.

sentences.zh: 常為高祖參乘，以舍人從起沛。

translations.literal: He often served Gaozu as chariot companion and followed him as a retainer when he arose from Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly served as Gaozu's chariot companion and followed him as a retainer when he first rose at Pei.

sentences.zh: 至霸上，西入蜀、漢，還定三秦，食邑池陽。

translations.literal: He arrived at Bashang, went west into Shu and Han, returned and pacified the Three Qins, and received the fief of Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign carried him to Bashang, west into Shu and Han, and back to pacify the Three Qin kingdoms; he then received the revenue fief of Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 東絕甬道，從出度平陰，遇淮陰侯兵襄國，軍乍利乍不利，終無離上心。

translations.literal: He cut off the eastern Yongdao, followed and emerged crossing Pingyin, encountered the Marquis of Huaiyin's troops at Xiangguo. The army was now advantageous, now disadvantageous, but he finally had no heart that departed from the Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: After cutting the eastern corridor road, he crossed Pingyin on campaign and met the Marquis of Huaiyin's forces at Xiangguo. Though the army's fortunes swung between victory and defeat, he never wavered in his devotion to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 以緤為信武侯，食邑三千三百戶。

translations.literal: Xie was made Marquis of Xinwu, with a food fief of three thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was made Marquis of Xinwu and granted a revenue fief of three thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖十二年，以緤為蒯成侯，除前所食邑。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's twelfth year, Xie was made Marquis of Kuaicheng, with previous fiefs eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Gaozu's reign, Xie was made Marquis of Kuaicheng, superseding all previous fiefs.

sentences.zh: 上欲自擊陳豨，蒯成侯泣曰：「始秦攻破天下，未嘗自行。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to attack Chen Xi in person, the Marquis of Kuaicheng wept and said, "When Qin first overran the realm, its ruler never took the field in person.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wanted to lead the attack on Chen Xi himself, the Marquis of Kuaicheng wept and said, "When Qin first conquered the realm, its ruler never personally took the field.

sentences.zh: 今上常自行，是為無人可使者乎？」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty constantly campaigns in person—does this mean there is no one who can be sent to do the work?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet now Your Majesty is forever campaigning in person. Are there truly no men who can be sent instead?"

sentences.zh: 上以為「愛我」，賜入殿門不趨，殺人不死。

translations.literal: The emperor took this as "love for me" and granted him entry through the palace gate without quick-stepping, and that homicide would not be punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as "loving me" and granted him entry through the palace gate without quick-stepping, and immunity from the death penalty for homicide.

sentences.zh: 至孝文五年，緤以壽終，謚為貞侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Emperor Wen's reign, Xie died of old age and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Xie died of old age and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子昌代侯，有罪，國除。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded as marquis, but had a crime and his state was eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded to the marquisate but was found guilty of a crime, and his state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 至孝景中二年，封緤子居代侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of the middle reign period of Emperor Jing, Xie's son Ju was enfeoffed as successor marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Jing's middle reign period, Xie's son Ju was enfeoffed to continue the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 至元鼎三年，居為太常，有罪，國除。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanding, Ju served as Grand Supplicator but had a crime, and his state was eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yuanding era, Ju was serving as Grand Master of Ceremonies when he was found guilty of a crime, and his state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：陽陵侯傅寬、信武侯靳歙皆高爵，從高祖起山東，攻項籍，誅殺名將，破軍降城以十數，未嘗困辱，此亦天授也。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: The Marquis of Yangling Fu Kuan and the Marquis of Xinwu Jin Xi both held high noble ranks. They followed Gaozu in rising from Shandong, attacked Xiang Ji, executed famous generals, broke armies, and induced the surrender of cities numbering in the tens, and never experienced distress or humiliation. This too was heaven's bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: The Marquis of Yangling, Fu Kuan, and the Marquis of Xinwu, Jin Xi, both held high noble ranks. They followed Gaozu in rising from Shandong, attacked Xiang Ji, executed famous generals, broke armies, and induced the surrender of cities numbering in the tens, and never experienced distress or humiliation. This too was heaven's bestowal.

sentences.zh: 蒯成侯周緤操心堅正，身不見疑，上欲有所之，未嘗不垂涕，此有傷心者然，可謂篤厚君子矣。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Zhou Xie, held a heart that was firm and upright, and his person was never suspected. Whenever the emperor intended to go on campaign, he never failed to shed tears. This was the bearing of one whose heart was wounded for his lord. He may be called a man of deep and genuine devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Zhou Xie, was steadfast and upright in his convictions, and his loyalty was never called into question. Whenever the sovereign intended to take the field, Xie never failed to weep. His was the bearing of one whose heart truly ached for his lord. He may well be called a man of deep and genuine devotion.
